items.title: Define versioned prompt contract schemas and deterministic digest algorithms
items.context: Add RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptEnvelope, PromptMeasurementRecord, and usage observation structures with pinned canonical serialization, line, byte, token-estimator, and repetition algorithms. Story 1 defines PromptEnvelope but must never instantiate a Story-bound envelope.
items.userSees: The CLI can report the exact contract and measurement algorithm versions used for the baseline.
excludes: full or incremental Task Context assembly

happy.desc: A focused contract smoke imports RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptMeasurementRecord, and PromptEnvelope, validates their exact proofbound.*.v1 schema discriminators and required digest/version/binding fields, and also validates the DispatchUsageObservation shape without granting it Story or reviewer authority.

The exported contract metadata names and pins the canonical-serialization, UTF-8 byte, LF logical-line, token-estimator, and repetition algorithms/versions; the same structured value and prompt text produce byte-identical canonical bytes, digests, bytes, lines, token estimates, and repetition results across repeated calls.

Token estimation reuses the existing usage-ledger bytesCharsEstimator contract (bytes-chars-heuristic version 1, utf8-bytes) and matches its empty, ASCII, CJK, and emoji results; Story 1 does not fork the estimator formula or mint a competing version.

edge.desc: Canonical serialization recursively orders object keys by a pinned ordinal/Unicode-code-point rule independent of insertion order and locale, preserves array order and Unicode scalar content without implicit normalization, and yields identical bytes/digests for insertion-order variants while distinguishing intentionally different Unicode sequences.

Tests pin LF logical-line behavior for empty text, one line, trailing LF, multiple LF separators, and CRLF input, while UTF-8 byte measurement remains the raw final text bytes; normalized line semantics and raw-byte/assembled-prompt digests are separate and cannot be substituted for one another.

Every semantic, render, assembled-prompt, measurement, and envelope/content-address digest is SHA-256 over a documented versioned domain plus canonical bytes; changing only the digest purpose/domain or algorithm/schema version changes the digest, preventing a digest from one field from being replayed as another.

The repetition metric pins normalization, shingle/matching behavior, denominator/empty-input behavior, ordering, and an explicit algorithm version; repeated and no-repetition fixtures have reproducible bounded results and a version change is observable in contract metadata.

adversarial.desc: Canonical serialization and digest entry points reject rather than omit/coerce undefined (including nested object/array values), NaN, positive/negative Infinity, unsupported values, sparse/cyclic structures, or otherwise non-canonical input; no invalid value can collapse to null, disappear, or produce an admissible digest.

Mutation probes reject missing required fields, unknown schema/algorithm versions, malformed digest values, invalid status/context/dispatch enums, non-finite or negative measurements, and inconsistent envelope bindings instead of applying permissive defaults.

Repository/runtime probes prove Story 1 defines and validates the PromptEnvelope type/schema only: the measurement report and baseline emit PromptMeasurementRecord sidecars, never instantiate or persist a Story-bound PromptEnvelope, never mint envelopeId/reviewRun authority, and do not alter full/incremental assembly or review-pass gates.

verificationEvidence.note: Typed v1 contracts and DispatchUsageObservation validate in the focused smoke at commit bac0da352b.
Repeated serialization, digest, metric, and repetition fixtures are deterministic.
Empty, ASCII, CJK, and emoji estimates equal usage-ledger bytesCharsEstimator v1.
Recursive code-point key order is insertion independent and Unicode sequences remain distinct.
Empty, trailing LF, multiple LF, CRLF, ASCII, CJK, and emoji boundaries pass.
Domain and version mutation produce distinct SHA-256 digests.
Five-token shingle algorithm metadata, no-repeat, repeat, bounds, and deterministic fixtures pass.
Undefined, nonfinite, unsupported, sparse, cyclic, and non-plain values are rejected.
Unknown schema/status, malformed digest, negative/nonfinite metrics, and inconsistent bindings reject.
Story 1 exposes only the type/validator and test fixtures; there is no builder, writer, report instance, persistence, or gate integration.

items.title: Freeze the canonical lifecycle registry for all 16 prompt roles
items.context: Use the current package prompt registry as the exact role set. Record active, compatibility, and retired states plus replacements/defaultDispatch without changing current legal dispatch behavior; channel is retired, product-reviewer remains active INIT authority, implementation-reviewer is compatibility, and legacy verification names point to verification-intent.
items.userSees: The role report lists exactly 16 roles and clearly separates active, compatibility, and retired roles.

happy.desc: The lifecycle registry enumerates exactly the 16 package prompt-registry role IDs with no additions or omissions: implementation-reviewer, lattice-evaluator, lattice-evaluator-cli, lattice-implementer, lattice-review-behavior, lattice-review-channel, lattice-review-concept, lattice-review-delivery, lattice-review-docs, lattice-review-quality, lattice-review-scope-plan, lattice-review-story-init, lattice-review-test-coverage, product-reviewer, test-case-reviewer, and test-intent; each row has an explicit valid lifecycle status and defaultDispatch boolean.

The exact lifecycle partition is 12 active roles (all exact members other than the three compatibility roles and retired channel), compatibility={implementation-reviewer,test-case-reviewer,test-intent}, retired={lattice-review-channel}; channel is retired with defaultDispatch=false and is excluded from the active count.

product-reviewer remains active and its existing INIT-only independent init_check_set authority is unchanged; implementation-reviewer remains compatibility/non-default with migration guidance to the existing quality+behavior combination and does not acquire a new REVIEW lane; test-intent and test-case-reviewer are compatibility/non-default and each declares canonical replacementAgentType=verification-intent.

edge.desc: Membership comparison is order-independent but exact: sorting the lifecycle registry IDs equals sorting readPromptRegistry().agents IDs, and active+compatibility+retired counts sum to 16 with mutually exclusive membership.
Compatibility and retired rows are present in reporting rather than silently dropped; their defaultDispatch values are false, and active-role reporting does not count them.

Existing dispatch resolution is behaviorally unchanged across canonical types and aliases: test-intent and test-case-reviewer still normalize to verification-intent with the same PLAN/item target, permissions, and prompt builder; product-reviewer retains INIT/story-only authority; no lifecycle metadata creates implementation-reviewer dispatch authority.

The existing lattice-review-channel dispatch route remains byte/behavior compatible in Story 1 even though lifecycle metadata reports it retired; retirement is descriptive in this baseline Story and does not prematurely implement the later dispatch rejection milestone.

adversarial.desc: A lifecycle registry definition containing a duplicate role ID fails closed with a typed/explicit validation error rather than deduplicating or choosing one row.
A lifecycle registry definition missing any one of the 16 package prompt roles fails closed, including compatibility or retired roles; it cannot report a partial registry as valid.
A lifecycle registry definition containing an unknown seventeenth role fails closed; prefix similarity, case folding, or an unregistered alias cannot manufacture lifecycle authority.

Invalid lifecycle status, missing defaultDispatch, compatibility rows without required replacement/migration metadata, or retired channel with defaultDispatch=true fail closed rather than being normalized into a permissive state.

A before/after snapshot of AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY accepted names, aliases, allowed phases, target cardinality, prompt builders, mutation permissions, reviewer lanes, and default lattice-implementer routing is identical; lifecycle registry introduction cannot alter current dispatch routing or evidence authority.

items.title: Expose a reproducible three-layer prompt measurement report and sidecar baseline
items.context: Add a read-only report for bytes, lines, estimated tokens, repetition, assembledPromptTokens, knownDispatchInputTokens availability, and providerProcessedInputTokens availability. The no-Story baseline must use PromptMeasurementRecord and honestly mark unobserved provider input unavailable.
items.userSees: Running the measurement command prints per-role and aggregate costs with unavailable fields shown explicitly instead of zero.

happy.desc: Run prompt_measurement_report in text mode without a Story: output lists exactly the canonical 16 roles plus an aggregate summary, and every role and aggregate exposes bytes, lines, estimatedTokens, and the versioned repetition metric together with the assembled, known-dispatch, and provider-processed input-layer availability boundaries.

Run prompt_measurement_report in JSON mode: it is machine-parseable and contains the same canonical role set, per-role metrics, aggregate metrics, algorithm/schema versions, layer meanings, and availability states as text mode; recomputing from current agent_prompt outputs reproduces all assembled bytes, lines, estimated-token, digest, and repetition values.

The checked-in role-prompt measurement sidecar uses proofbound.prompt-measurement.v1 PromptMeasurementRecord entries for all 16 roles, records the pinned contract/digest/estimator metadata and aggregate report data without creating PromptEnvelope authority, and two runs from identical inputs produce byte-identical canonical JSON and the same digest.

edge.desc: Metric boundary probes cover UTF-8 multibyte content, trailing versus non-trailing newline line counts, deterministic token-estimator rounding, and repeated versus unique normalized content; per-role values and aggregate totals/repetition follow the pinned algorithms with no host-locale or clock-dependent drift.

assembledPromptTokens is always reported as the locally reproducible layer, while knownDispatchInputTokens and providerProcessedInputTokens each carry an independent availability result: observing one layer must not make the other appear observed, and unavailable optional token/cache components are not included in totals.

The report is usable without storyId in INIT, INIT_CHECK, PLAN, DEV, REVIEW, TEST, and DONE contexts and returns the same measurement for the same registry inputs; phase, owner, review-run, HEAD, or Story metadata is neither required nor used to mint a Story-bound PromptEnvelope or lifecycle evidence.

Command catalog, registry, command policy, config, and activity policy classify prompt_measurement_report as a read-only, all-phase command; process-fact registration is exactly L0 observational and cannot be consumed as review, validation, budget-waiver, or lifecycle gate evidence.

adversarial.desc: With no observable launcher/provider usage, both text and JSON explicitly report known-dispatch and provider-processed layers as unavailable; they never emit numeric 0, silently omit the availability state, copy assembled estimates into those fields, or imply hidden system-wrapper/cache coverage.

Instrument provider and host-launcher call seams to fail if invoked: prompt_measurement_report still succeeds using only local registry/prompt data and makes zero provider, model, network, or dispatch calls.

Compare repository material, Story/checklist/review facts, process evidence, runtime artifacts, baseline file, and activity state before and after both output modes: the report performs no writes and does not refresh, accept, or mutate the sidecar baseline.

Remove, duplicate, rename, or add a registry role and corrupt a measurement or PromptMeasurementRecord field: generation/verification fails closed instead of silently producing fewer or more than 16 rows, stale aggregate values, a partial sidecar, or a fresh-looking deterministic digest.

Attempt to use the L0 prompt measurement process fact as a reviewer receipt, review pass, validation result, budget approval/waiver, or phase-transition artifact: every gate rejects it while the observational report remains available.

items.title: Prove all existing prompt outputs remain byte-identical and new registries fail closed
items.context: Extend focused smokes/verifiers so all 16 agent_prompt hashes and bytes remain unchanged, role membership/status/replacements are exact, canonical digest changes are detected, missing contract fields fail, and measurement output is deterministic.
items.userSees: Focused verification reports all 16 existing Prompt outputs unchanged while contract and measurement mutation probes fail closed.
excludes: rewriting Prompt bodies to satisfy budgets

happy.desc: Run the existing Proof-or-Stop baseline verifier in read-only mode and prove the canonical registry still contains exactly the same 16 roles, with every generated agent_prompt byte count and whole-output SHA-256 equal to the pre-Story baseline; the verifier must offer no hash-refresh path and docs/requirements/baselines/proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.json must remain byte-identical.

Build packages/main, run the focused prompt-contract/measurement smoke, and run scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.mjs successfully; two measurements of the same pinned inputs must serialize to byte-identical output with identical aggregate and per-role values.

edge.desc: Assert the role registry has exactly 16 unique canonical role IDs and exact lifecycle metadata for boundary cases: lattice-review-channel is retired and non-default, product-reviewer is active INIT authority, implementation-reviewer is compatibility, and test-intent/test-case-reviewer replace or alias to canonical verification-intent without changing currently legal dispatch behavior.

For all 16 roles, compare both source template output and the two generated mirror surfaces against the pre-implementation tree; git diff must be empty for packages/main templates, .lattice-codex/agents, and .claude/agents, including newline and final-byte differences.

Exercise canonical serialization at boundary values (empty optional observations, unavailable known/provider input, multibyte text and newline-sensitive byte/line counts): repeated equivalent input must keep the same digest and measurement, while a semantically relevant contract-field change must change the canonical digest.

adversarial.desc: Mutation probes must fail closed when any required RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptEnvelope, or PromptMeasurementRecord field is absent, when schemaVersion is unknown, or when lifecycle status/replacement/defaultDispatch violates the frozen role policy; no partial registry or permissive fallback is accepted.

Tampering with canonical contract data, semantic/render/assembled digests, bytes, lines, estimated tokens, repetition values, or unavailable usage markers must be detected by the focused smoke/verifier rather than normalized away or reported as a passing measurement.

A controlled temporary mutation of one of the 16 assembled Prompt outputs must make the baseline verifier fail on exact bytes/hash, and restoring the source must restore PASS; accepting or refreshing the baseline hash to hide that drift is explicitly forbidden and the repository baseline/templates/mirrors must finish with an empty diff.
